chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There are two things in which most people are tested/tempted: health and leisure.
ai.seo_question: What are the two things that cause most people to be tested according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this Prophetic tradition to emphasize that physical well-being and unoccupied time are not merely blessings but tests of spiritual vigilance. This insight aligns with the Shia ethical focus on *muraqabah* (self-monitoring), urging believers to actively channel their vitality and leisure into worship and good deeds to avoid the heedlessness (*ghaflah*) that often accompanies ease.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-6 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“There are two things which cause trouble for most people: health and leisure.”
